_README: The machines this Gateway is allowed to look at, and the only ones it can.
Copy this file to remote-targets.json beside it, or point REMOTE_TARGETS_FILE
anywhere you like. The real file is NOT tracked: it names hosts, addresses and
paths, which are properties of one deployment rather than of the code, and
gateway/remote.py deliberately contains none of them.
Diagnosis is read-only. Nothing in the services, channels or ssh.checks blocks
can start, stop or change anything - the ssh checks are run verbatim and their
output is reported, so a command that modifies the far end is the one way to
break that, and it is your responsibility not to write one.
THE 'recovery' BLOCK IS THE EXCEPTION, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE. Commands listed
there are meant to change the far end, and gateway/recovery.py will run one on
a human's explicit confirmation. Everything else about them is a restriction.
FIELDS
name        what to call it in a question. This is what the assistant passes
to remote_diagnose; it cannot pass an address.
label       how it should be read aloud.
hostname    the tailnet name, used to look the peer up in `tailscale status`.
host        the address probes connect to. A tailnet IP or a DNS name.
services    ports to try. health_path is optional; without one only the TCP
connect is attempted, which proves a listener and nothing more.
channels    files an agent on that machine writes. This is the only evidence
available for an agent that has no port. They are stat'd on THIS
host and reported as such - a synced file is not the remote disk.
ssh         optional. Without it the report says plainly that the process
table, PIDs, directories and remote logs were not measured.
checks are named read-only commands; none are built in, because a
built-in one would assume the remote operating system.
An ssh block is also what recovery needs: without one, every
recovery action on this machine refuses, because there is no way
to run anything on it from here.
RECOVERY FIELDS (per action)
name              what the assistant names when asking to run it. Quoted back
to the operator verbatim, so write it as a sentence a person
would say yes to.
description       what it actually does, in the words you want read aloud
before somebody confirms it.
command           run verbatim over ssh. Written by you. There are no built-in
recovery commands and there will not be: one would assume the
far end's operating system, its service manager and its paths.
when.service      the service (by its name above) whose state justifies this.
Omit to judge on the machine's connectivity instead.
when.states       the states in which this action may run, from the diagnosis'
own vocabulary: 'not listening', 'listening but not
answering', 'listening', 'answering' for a service;
'reachable', 'unreachable', 'unknown' for a machine.
AN ACTION WITH NO when, OR NO STATES, CAN NEVER RUN. That is
deliberate and it fails closed: an unconditional action is a
remote shell rather than a recovery.
cooldown_minutes  how long before this action may run again. Default 15. A
restart that has not had time to take effect looks exactly
like one that did not work.
max_per_day       how many times in 24 hours. Default 4. A service needing more
has a problem a restart does not fix, and continuing hides it.
Every attempt is appended to remote-recovery-journal.jsonl beside this file
(or REMOTE_RECOVERY_JOURNAL). The cooldown and the ceiling are counted from it,
so if it cannot be written, recovery refuses rather than acting without a limit.

channels.name: the shared conversation
channels.path: C:\path\to\a\file the remote agent appends to.md
channels.description: What writes it, and what its silence would mean.

checks.name: the process
checks.command: the read-only command that lists it

actions.name: restart the gateway
actions.description: Restarts the gateway service and leaves everything else alone.
actions.command: the read-only-safe command that restarts just that service

actions.name: start the engineer session
actions.description: Starts the agent session that reads the shared channel.
actions.command: the command that launches it, non-interactively
